questions.stem: The branch of mining concerned with recovering minerals from loose river sands and gravels is
questions.explanation: Alluvial (placer) mining works loose deposits laid down by rivers.

questions.stem: The iron ore that supplies the Ajaokuta Steel Company is mined mainly at
questions.explanation: Itakpe iron ore in Kogi State was developed to feed Ajaokuta.

questions.stem: Lead and zinc ores have long been worked by artisanal and small-scale miners around
questions.explanation: The Benue Trough lead-zinc belt includes the Abakaliki/Enyigba area of Ebonyi State.

questions.stem: Gold, tin and gemstones are classified as
options: energy minerals like coal and uranium
industrial rocks such as limestone only
questions.explanation: Gold and tin are metallic minerals; gemstones form a separate valuable class.

questions.stem: Under the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007, the title that permits a holder to carry out large-scale extraction of minerals is the
questions.explanation: A mining lease authorises full-scale mining; reconnaissance permits and exploration licences are for earlier stages.

questions.stem: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), which agrees production quotas among member states, is an example of a
questions.explanation: A cartel is a group of producers that coordinate output and prices.

questions.stem: A quarry project costs ₦600 million and is expected to make a net profit of ₦90 million a year. The annual return on investment is
Quartz and feldspars are so common in crustal rocks because the two elements that make up about three-quarters of the crust by mass are
questions.explanation: The crust is about 46% oxygen and 28% silicon; together they form the silicate minerals such as quartz and feldspar.

questions.stem: The thin outermost solid layer of the Earth is the
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin rocky skin above the mantle.

questions.stem: A mineral can be scratched by a fingernail and feels soapy. Its Mohs hardness is most likely
questions.explanation: A fingernail (about 2.5) scratches talc, which is 1 on the Mohs scale and feels soapy.

questions.stem: Sandstone and shale are formed by the compaction and cementation of sediments. They are therefore
questions.explanation: Rocks built from deposited and cemented sediments are sedimentary.

questions.stem: Basalt is a fine-grained igneous rock because it
options: cooled quickly at or near the surface
formed from the shells of sea animals on the sea bed
was squeezed by heat and pressure
questions.explanation: Rapid cooling of lava allows little time for crystals to grow.

questions.stem: Shale changing to slate under heat and pressure is an example of
questions.explanation: Metamorphism alters existing rock in the solid state.

questions.stem: Rocks shattered by repeated heating during the day and cooling at night in desert areas of northern Nigeria undergo
questions.explanation: Expansion and contraction from temperature changes break rocks without changing their chemistry.

questions.stem: On a geological cross-section, a younger dyke cutting across older layers shows the principle of
options: faunal succession of fossils in layers
questions.explanation: Any feature that cuts through rocks must be younger than the rocks it cuts.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: The stage of mining that DEFINES the size, shape and grade of a deposit already discovered is
questions.explanation: Prospecting finds indications; exploration measures and delineates the deposit.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Taking soil and stream-sediment samples to analyse for traces of metals is a
questions.explanation: Geochemical methods measure chemical traces in soils, sediments, water or plants.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Satellite images used to map rock types and structures over a wide area are an example of
questions.explanation: Remote sensing gathers data without contact, from aircraft or satellites.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: A company has found a huge, low-grade copper deposit only 30 m below flat farmland. The mining approach MOST likely to be chosen is
options: block caving from a deep shaft
questions.explanation: Shallow, large, low-grade orebodies can be worked cheaply from surface; underground methods suit deep or narrow ones.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Extracting copper by passing electric current through a solution so that pure metal deposits on the cathode is
questions.explanation: Electrometallurgy uses electricity to deposit or refine metal.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Smelting of ores in a furnace at high temperature is classified as
questions.explanation: Pyro means fire; smelting and roasting are pyrometallurgical.

questions.topic: Stages of Development in Mining (Basic Concepts)
questions.stem: Which of these is a unit operation in mining (rather than mineral processing)?
questions.explanation: Mining unit operations are drilling, blasting, loading and hauling; the others are processing operations.

questions.stem: Granite aggregate for road construction is produced mainly by
questions.explanation: Quarries extract and crush rock for aggregates.

questions.stem: In one year a pit hauls 3.6 million tonnes of rock in total, of which 0.6 million tonnes is ore. The stripping ratio (waste : ore) is
questions.explanation: Waste = 3.6 - 0.6 = 3.0 Mt; stripping ratio = 3.0/0.6 = 5 : 1 (6 : 1 wrongly uses total rock).

questions.stem: Blocks of granite or marble cut to size for building and monuments are called
questions.explanation: Dimension stone is quarried in blocks and slabs of specified size.

questions.stem: A block of ore 20 m long, 10 m wide and 5 m deep has a density of 2.7 t/m³. Its mass is
questions.explanation: Volume = 1000 m³; mass = 1000 x 2.7 = 2700 t.

questions.stem: The horizontal steps cut in the walls of an open pit are called
questions.explanation: Benches give safe slopes and working platforms.

questions.stem: A vertical opening from the surface used to hoist ore and men in an underground mine is a
questions.explanation: A shaft is vertical or steeply inclined from surface; an adit is horizontal.

questions.stem: In cut-and-fill stoping, the mined-out space is
options: left completely empty so that air can circulate freely
backfilled to support walls and give a floor
questions.explanation: Backfill supports the walls and gives miners a floor for the next slice.

questions.stem: Block caving is suited to orebodies that are
options: near the surface in loose sand
large and weak enough to break under their own weight
questions.explanation: In block caving the undercut ore collapses by gravity and is drawn from below; it needs large, caveable orebodies.

questions.stem: Longwall mining is MOST commonly used for
questions.explanation: Longwall shearers work long faces in flat, uniform coal seams.

questions.topic: Other Mining Methods and Materials Handling
questions.stem: The machine with a large front bucket used to load broken rock into trucks at a mine is a
questions.explanation: Front-end (pay) loaders scoop and load material.

questions.topic: Other Mining Methods and Materials Handling
questions.stem: Space agencies are interested in mining asteroids mainly because some asteroids
options: are close enough to reach by road
contain metals and water that could be used in space
questions.explanation: Some asteroids are rich in metals such as nickel and platinum-group metals, and in water ice.

questions.topic: Other Mining Methods and Materials Handling
questions.stem: Large trucks that carry ore from the pit to the crusher are examples of
questions.explanation: Haul trucks, conveyors and loaders move materials.

questions.stem: A crusher reduces ore from 300 mm to 50 mm. The reduction ratio is
questions.explanation: Reduction ratio = feed size/product size = 300/50 = 6.

questions.stem: A magnetic separator is used to concentrate
questions.explanation: Magnetite is strongly magnetic and is removed from non-magnetic gangue.

A gemstone weighs 3.5 carats. Its mass in grams is
The instrument used to measure the refractive index of a cut gemstone is the
questions.explanation: A gem refractometer reads the refractive index, a key identification property.

questions.stem: The 2010 outbreak in Zamfara State that killed many children was caused by
options: lead poisoning from processing lead-rich gold ore in homes
questions.explanation: Artisanal gold ore rich in lead was crushed in villages; lead dust poisoned children.

questions.stem:
(a) State five reasons why minerals are important to the Nigerian economy. [5 marks]
(b) Name the type of mineral title under the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, 2007 that a person needs to (i) carry out preliminary search over a wide area, (ii) explore a defined area in detail, (iii) carry out large-scale mining. [6 marks]
(c) Name three sources of finance for a mining venture. [3 marks]
(d) Name three minerals found in Nigeria and a state where each is found. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) any five: foreign exchange, raw materials for industry, employment, government revenue, infrastructure development, diversification of economy (1 each)
2 marks: (b)(i) reconnaissance permit
2 marks: (b)(ii) exploration licence
2 marks: (b)(iii) mining lease
3 marks: (c) any three: equity/shares, bank loans, government grants/intervention funds, retained earnings, joint venture partners (1 each)
6 marks: (d) any three correct pairs: coal–Enugu/Kogi; tin–Plateau; iron ore–Kogi; limestone–Ogun/Kogi/Cross River; lead-zinc–Ebonyi; gold–Zamfara/Osun/Niger; bitumen–Ondo; barite–Nasarawa/Taraba (2 each)
questions.explanation: Minerals bring revenue, jobs and raw materials. Titles: reconnaissance permit, exploration licence, mining lease. Finance from equity, loans, grants. Examples: coal (Enugu), tin (Plateau), iron ore (Kogi).

questions.stem:
(a) With the aid of a description, explain the internal structure of the Earth. [8 marks]
(b) Distinguish between physical and chemical weathering, giving two examples of each. [8 marks]
(c) State four physical properties used to identify rock-forming minerals. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) crust: thin outer layer, continental and oceanic, 5–70 km
2 marks: (a) mantle: thick layer of hot silicate rock to about 2900 km
2 marks: (a) outer core: liquid iron-nickel
2 marks: (a) inner core: solid iron-nickel at very high temperature/pressure
2 marks: (b) physical: breaking of rock without chemical change
2 marks: (b) examples: temperature changes/exfoliation, frost action, root wedging, abrasion (any two)
2 marks: (b) chemical: change in mineral composition by reactions
2 marks: (b) examples: oxidation, hydrolysis, carbonation, solution (any two)
4 marks: (c) any four: colour, streak, lustre, hardness, cleavage/fracture, specific gravity, crystal form (1 each)
questions.explanation: The Earth has crust, mantle, liquid outer core and solid inner core. Physical weathering breaks rock mechanically; chemical weathering changes minerals by oxidation, hydrolysis, carbonation. Minerals are identified by colour, streak, lustre, hardness, cleavage, SG.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the unit operations in a granite quarry, from the face to the stockpile. [8 marks]
(b) An open pit has an annual ore production of 1.2 million tonnes and a stripping ratio of 3.5 : 1. Calculate (i) the waste removed per year, (ii) the total material moved per year. [6 marks]
(c) State three advantages of surface mining over underground mining. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) drilling of blast holes on the bench
2 marks: (a) blasting with explosives to break rock
2 marks: (a) loading with excavators/loaders and hauling with trucks
2 marks: (a) crushing and screening into sizes, then stockpiling
3 marks: (b)(i) waste = 3.5 x 1.2 = 4.2 million tonnes
3 marks: (b)(ii) total = 4.2 + 1.2 = 5.4 million tonnes
6 marks: (c) any three: lower cost per tonne, higher production rate, safer working, better recovery, easier use of large machines, better ventilation/light (2 each)
questions.explanation: Quarry: drill, blast, load and haul, crush and screen, stockpile. Waste = 4.2 Mt, total 5.4 Mt. Surface mining is cheaper, faster, safer with higher recovery.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of the following underground mine openings: (i) shaft, (ii) adit, (iii) stope, (iv) raise. [8 marks]
(b) Describe the shrinkage stoping method. [6 marks]
(c) Compare surface and underground mining under three headings. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) shaft: vertical/inclined opening from surface for access, hoisting, ventilation
2 marks: (a)(ii) adit: horizontal tunnel driven from a hillside into the mine
2 marks: (a)(iii) stope: excavation from which ore is mined
2 marks: (a)(iv) raise: opening driven upwards from a lower level
2 marks: (b) ore mined in horizontal slices upward from below
2 marks: (b) broken ore left in stope as working floor; only swell portion (about one-third) drawn
2 marks: (b) when stope complete, remaining ore drawn; suits steep, strong orebodies and walls
6 marks: (c) any three headings compared: cost, depth of deposit, safety, recovery, environmental impact, production rate (2 each)
questions.explanation: Shaft vertical, adit horizontal from hillside, stope is the ore excavation, raise driven upward. Shrinkage stoping mines upward, leaving broken ore as a floor and drawing the swell. Surface mining is cheaper and safer; underground suits deep deposits with less surface disturbance.

questions.stem:
(a) Define (i) comminution, (ii) concentration, (iii) tailings. [6 marks]
(b) A plant treats 400 t of ore assaying 2.5% Sn and produces 13 t of concentrate assaying 65% Sn. Calculate (i) the ratio of concentration, (ii) the recovery of tin, (iii) the mass of tin lost in tailings. [9 marks]
(c) State two methods of disposing of tailings safely. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) comminution: size reduction by crushing and grinding to liberate minerals
2 marks: (a)(ii) concentration: separating valuable minerals from gangue to increase grade
2 marks: (a)(iii) tailings: waste product after concentration
3 marks: (b)(i) ratio of concentration = 400/13 = 30.8
3 marks: (b)(ii) tin in feed = 10 t; tin in concentrate = 8.45 t; recovery = 84.5%
3 marks: (b)(iii) tin lost = 10 - 8.45 = 1.55 t
5 marks: (c) any two described: engineered tailings dam with lining, dry stacking after dewatering, backfilling underground, revegetation of dumps (2.5 each, award 3+2)
questions.explanation: Ratio = 400/13 = 30.8. Tin in feed 10 t, in concentrate 8.45 t, recovery 84.5%, loss 1.55 t. Tailings disposed in lined dams, dry stacks or as backfill.

questions.stem:
(a) List five items of personal protective equipment used in mining and state the use of each. [10 marks]
(b) Describe five steps a mine should take to control environmental damage. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) hard hat: protects head from falling rock
2 marks: (a) safety boots: protect feet
2 marks: (a) dust mask/respirator: prevents inhalation of dust
2 marks: (a) ear defenders: prevent hearing loss from noise
2 marks: (a) cap lamp/goggles/reflective vest: light/eye protection/visibility (any one)
2 marks: (b) carry out Environmental Impact Assessment before mining
2 marks: (b) control dust by water spraying
2 marks: (b) treat mine water and tailings before discharge
2 marks: (b) backfill pits and re-vegetate land (reclamation)
2 marks: (b) monitor air, water, noise and report to regulators
questions.explanation: PPE: hard hat, boots, respirator, ear defenders, cap lamp. Environmental control: EIA, dust suppression, water treatment, reclamation, monitoring.
